title: Connection pool exhausted during a retry storm
context_text: A brief database blip causes clients to retry, the retries amplify, and the pool is starved long after the original fault cleared
solution_text: Bound retries with jittered exponential backoff and set a pool acquisition timeout so callers fail fast instead of queueing. Add a circuit breaker so a sustained fault stops generating load.
source: public: well-documented cascading-failure pattern; see AWS Architecture Blog on exponential backoff and jitter

title: Floating point used for money
context_text: Totals drift by fractions of a cent and reconciliation fails, because amounts were stored and summed as floats
solution_text: Store money as integer minor units or a fixed-point decimal type. Never use binary floating point for currency arithmetic.
source: public: IEEE 754 cannot represent most decimal fractions exactly; standard financial-systems guidance

title: N+1 queries from lazy ORM relationship access
context_text: A list endpoint issues one query per row because a related object is accessed inside the loop, so latency scales with result size
solution_text: Eager-load the relation in the initial query, or batch-load related rows by id in one round trip.
source: public: N+1 select problem is documented across Hibernate, ActiveRecord and SQLAlchemy

title: Missing index on a foreign key column
context_text: Deletes on the parent table get slower as the child table grows, because each delete scans the child to enforce the constraint
solution_text: Index the referencing column. Most databases index the primary key side automatically but not the referencing side.
source: public: PostgreSQL documentation notes that referencing columns are not indexed automatically

title: ADD COLUMN NOT NULL fails on a populated table
context_text: A migration that adds a non-nullable column succeeds on an empty test database and fails in production with 'column contains null values'
solution_text: Supply a server-side default so existing rows backfill, or add the column nullable, backfill, then set NOT NULL.
source: public: standard SQL DDL semantics; reproduced identically on PostgreSQL and MySQL

title: Schema migration locks a table during deploy
context_text: An index build or column rewrite takes an exclusive lock and blocks reads and writes for the duration on a large table
solution_text: Build indexes concurrently where the engine supports it, and split the change into expand, backfill, contract phases so the old and new application versions both work mid-migration.
source: public: PostgreSQL CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY documentation; expand/contract is standard practice

title: Offset pagination skips or repeats rows
context_text: Paging through a list with OFFSET returns duplicates or misses records when rows are inserted or deleted between pages
solution_text: Order by a total, stable key and paginate by cursor on that key. If OFFSET must be used, add a unique tiebreaker to the sort so the order is deterministic.
source: public: keyset vs offset pagination is well documented; ordering without a unique tiebreaker is not stable

title: Read-modify-write loses a concurrent update
context_text: Two processes read a record, each change a different field, and the second write silently reverts the first change
solution_text: Update the specific fields in the database rather than writing back a whole object, or use optimistic concurrency with a version column and retry on conflict.
source: public: lost update is a classic transaction anomaly, defined in the SQL standard's isolation discussion

title: Non-atomic check-then-insert races under concurrency
context_text: Code checks whether a row exists and inserts if not; under concurrent requests both checks pass and one insert violates a unique constraint
solution_text: Use an atomic upsert (INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE) so the database resolves the race, rather than racing two round trips against it.
source: public: PostgreSQL ON CONFLICT documentation exists specifically for this pattern

title: Counter increments lost under concurrent updates
context_text: A counter read into the application, incremented, and written back loses increments when requests overlap
solution_text: Increment in the database (SET n = n + 1) so the operation is atomic, instead of reading and writing from application memory.
source: public: standard consequence of read-modify-write without isolation

title: Timestamps stored without timezone information
context_text: Times are stored as naive local timestamps, so records written from hosts in different regions cannot be ordered or compared reliably
solution_text: Store instants in UTC with an explicit timezone-aware type, and convert only at the presentation boundary.
source: public: standard guidance; PostgreSQL timestamptz vs timestamp semantics

title: User input interpolated into a query string
context_text: Building SQL by concatenating request values allows an attacker to alter the query's structure
solution_text: Pass values as bound parameters so they can never be parsed as SQL. This applies to LIKE patterns and ORDER BY targets too, which need an allowlist rather than interpolation.

title: Sort order differs between database and application
context_text: Results ordered by the database appear in a different order after in-application sorting, because the collation differs from the language's default comparison
solution_text: Sort in one place, and set the collation explicitly where ordering is user-visible or paginated.
source: public: PostgreSQL and MySQL collation documentation; ICU vs byte ordering
